judge_input.description:
- improve the error handling that is currently in place so that it goes right ahead and logs each and every single one of the error types that there happen to be, without leaving even one of them out of it

Add in an error frame of its own, and go ahead and do that for absolutely all of the error types that exist, namely the ones that are listed out over at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/developers/guides/cookbooks/speech-to-text/streaming#error-handling 

- fix the issue that ends up coming up with the infinite loop, and the specific case in which that issue happens is the case where the websocket goes ahead and disconnects on its own
Explanation: the [_receive_messages](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/blob/7e424d750ebee48d8ff8af6f009b8257acd41dc5/src/pipecat/services/elevenlabs/stt.py#L693) method is one that ends up being executed from inside of a loop, and that loop is itself one which goes and makes an attempt to reconnect on whatever occasion it is that an error happens to come along. However, the eleven labs implementation exactly as it stood had a try catch sitting right there inside of it, and the direct consequence of that try catch being where it was is the following thing: in the event that the websocket happens to go and randomly disconnect entirely on its own, then this particular part of the whole thing goes right off into an infinite loop, and that infinite loop, once it has gotten itself going, is then the thing that goes on from there to block the whole entire process from managing to move along at all.

https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat/blob/7e424d750ebee48d8ff8af6f009b8257acd41dc5/src/pipecat/services/websocket_service.py#L133-L154
